# Dock pane header actions wear stock button chrome — a design pass for the four themes

## Context

The pane-header action family under epic #13158 shipped its semantics this cycle — `close`, `pin`, `maximize` (`#17952`/`#17953`) and the overflow-as-first-action (`#17960`) — and `#17956` shipped the `ui: 'inline' | 'standalone'` container variants with per-theme sheets. What never shipped, and was never ticketed, is the **visual design of the actions themselves** plus the theme values the inline variant reserved room for. The reference bar is the Qt-parity pane header: a compact cluster of flat monochrome glyphs sharing the strip's band, close at the corner — not a row of standalone buttons.

## The Problem

Measured at Engine `dev@9954179bb7` (post all four family merges):

- **The only action-specific CSS in the entire tree is the focus-gating carrier** (`.neo-toolbar-action-context-inactive`, `resources/scss/src/toolbar/Base.scss`). Every projected header action renders as a stock `neo-button` in whatever the active theme's default button chrome is — in the neo themes that is a large filled rounded button, visually dominating the header band it sits in. Witnessed in the `dock-maximize` component fixture (neo-theme-neo-dark: filled square buttons for close/maximize) and in `apps/workstation` (the `#17960` overflow control renders as a generic bordered button on the "Priority Alert Observatory" pane).
- **The inline gradient hook has no values.** `#17950` froze `--tab-header-inline-background-image`, consumed as `background-image: var(--tab-header-inline-background-image, none)` on `.neo-tab-container-inline > .neo-tab-header-toolbar` (`resources/scss/src/tab/Container.scss:6`) — and no theme value layer sets it, so the `none` default renders everywhere. The hook satisfied its ticket's ACs; the *design* (a subtle band gradient for dense pane headers) was deliberately left to a values pass that has no ticket.
- **`apps/workstation` never enables the engine actions.** The engine's own showcase inherits the inline chrome (six inline containers render today) but projects no close/pin/maximize — so the chrome this ticket designs has no living witness in a public app until the flags turn on there.

## The Architectural Reality

- Action items are addressable: every projected action carries `cls: 'neo-toolbar-action'` and `isToolbarAction: true` (`src/toolbar/Base.mjs:373,391`); contributions add `isToolbarActionContribution` (`#17960`). The chrome selector is therefore `.neo-tab-header-toolbar .neo-toolbar-action` (scoped to tab headers so ordinary toolbars keep their button chrome), with the gating carrier already handling shown/hidden interactivity.
- The four theme value layers exist and already carry tab sheets (`resources/scss/theme-{light,dark,neo-light,neo-dark}/tab/Container.scss`, extended by `#17956`) — the values land beside the variant styling they complete.
- The engine set is focus-gated by default; whatever hover/rest states the design chooses must keep the gated state's geometry-preserving discipline (the carrier toggles interactivity, not layout).

## The Fix

One SCSS-plus-witness pass, no JS behavior changes:

1. **Action glyph chrome** for `.neo-tab-header-toolbar .neo-toolbar-action` in the structural sheet (compact hit target, transparent rest background, glyph-first) with per-theme values in all four theme layers (glyph color, hover/active surfaces, close-affordance accent if the theme language wants one). The Qt-parity read: actions share the header band, they do not sit on it as buttons.
2. **Inline gradient values**: set `--tab-header-inline-background-image` in the two neo themes (the dense-pane band the hook was frozen for); the classic themes may opt for `none` deliberately — a written choice, not an accident of the default.
3. **`apps/workstation` enables `enableDockCloseAction`, `enableDockPinAction`, `enableDockMaximizeAction`** — the engine's showcase becomes the living witness for the chrome across both neo themes and exercises the full frozen ordering: [overflow] → [engine set, focus-gated] → [close, always last].

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.neo-tab-header-toolbar .neo-toolbar-action` | `src/toolbar/Base.mjs` action marker + tab-header scope | compact glyph-first chrome only inside tab headers; ordinary toolbars stay unchanged | existing stock button chrome outside the selector | structural SCSS intent comment | selector-contract spec + per-theme visual receipt |
| `--tab-header-inline-background-image` | #17950 / merged #17956 hook | real band gradient in both neo themes | classic themes explicitly declare `none` | per-theme inline-variant comment | computed-style assertion in all four themes |
| Workstation `enableDockCloseAction` / `enableDockPinAction` / `enableDockMaximizeAction` | `dashboard.dock.Workspace` public configs | showcase projects the frozen engine action set and ordering | flags remain opt-in elsewhere | Workstation config rationale | dense-tour + action-order/focus-gating witness |
| gated action state | `neo-toolbar-action-context-inactive` carrier | geometry preserved; quiet and non-interactive under the new chrome | existing hidden-carrier semantics | no new public docs | focused/unfocused rect stability + visual receipt |

The ledger changes visual/value and host opt-in surfaces only. It does not reopen action semantics. Classic-theme `none` is an explicit value, not reliance on the structural fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Header actions in tab headers render glyph-first compact chrome, visually distinct from standalone buttons, in all four themes (visual evidence beat per the epic's closure-gate discipline: recorded comparison or screenshot pair per theme).
- [ ] Ordinary (non-tab-header) toolbars keep today's action rendering byte-identically — the chrome is scoped to `.neo-tab-header-toolbar` (regression spec on the cls contract).
- [ ] The two neo themes set a real `--tab-header-inline-background-image` value; the classic themes' choice is written in their sheets as a deliberate line (value or documented `none`).
- [ ] `apps/workstation` projects close, pin and maximize; the dense tour still passes; the focus-gating carrier's geometry-preserving behavior is unchanged (no layout shift when actions gate in/out).
- [ ] The gated (context-inactive) state remains visually quiet under the new chrome in all four themes.

## Out of Scope

- Any action semantics, ordering, or gating behavior — all frozen and shipped by the family leaves.
- Redesigning the two `ui` variants themselves (`#17956` owns that shape); this ticket only supplies the values and the action chrome those variants were built to host.
- The private consumer workspaces — they inherit whatever the themes ship.

## Related

Parent: #13158. Completes the design half of: #17950/`#17956` (variants + hook), `#17952` (pin), `#17953` (maximize), `#17960` (overflow-as-action). Reference precedent for gated-state mechanics: `resources/scss/src/toolbar/Base.scss`.

- 2026-08-31T22:08:15Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `19d6bac` - "test(workstation): the overflow cap reserves the action cluster, not one control (#17988)

`dev` was red here: expected 251, received 203, a delta of exactly 2 x 24px.

The spec re-derived the cap from `toolbarWidth - controlWidth`, which was right when
the overflow control was the only trailing action. #17963 turned on close, pin and
maximize in `apps/workstation`, so the header now carries a 3 x 24px partition and the
plugin reserves all of it: 275 - 72 = 203. Production produced the correct number; the
identity named the wrong operand.

Every geometric assertion in the same test already passed — zero painted intersection,
box ends at the control edge, indicator spans the capped box, label ellipsizes. That is
what convicts the formula rather than the plugin, and it is why none of them changed.

The cluster is measured from the DOM, not a count times an assumed size, because the
partition is per-consumer and per-opt-in flag. Gated actions are counted: the
focus-gating carrier hides them with `visibility`, which preserves the box, so a tab
allowed to run under a quiet action would be covered the moment its pane takes focus —
counting only visible actions would pass today and re-introduce the covered-tab defect
this spec exists to guard.

Adds a staging guard that the partition holds more than one action, so the identity
cannot pass by degenerating back into the single-operand form it replaced.

Co-Authored-By: Vega <neo-opus-vega@neomjs.com>"
- 2026-08-31T22:08:43Z @neo-opus-vega cross-referenced by PR #17989
- 2026-08-31T23:14:40Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `d084cd3` - "fix(workstation): the palette bridge out-ranks the theme it sits under (#17984)

The bridge maps generic `--grid-*` / `--tab-*` primitives onto `--workstation-*`, and
21 of its 23 contested tokens resolved to theme values instead. The active-tab
indicator painted `#FFFFFF` where the instrument's accent is mint, grid borders
painted `--purple-800`, and `--grid-header-button-justify-content` lost `flex-end`
to `start` — one loss was layout, not colour.

The cause is a specificity contest the bridge was moved into. #15923 hoisted it from
`.workstation-workspace` to `.workstation-viewport` so the `?popout=` vessel could
reach it; the viewport carries the skin class, so `:root .neo-theme-*` (0,2,0) began
matching the same element as `.workstation-viewport` (0,1,0). The old scope was never
in that contest. Reachability bought, specificity lost.

Raising the viewport rule alone is not enough, because WHICH elements carry a skin
class is runtime state: `.neo-grid-container` carries one from boot, and
`.workstation-workspace` acquires one after a runtime skin switch. The nearest
declaring ancestor wins an inherited custom property outright, so any single pinned
element is one re-render from being shadowed again — exactly how the #15923 move
traded one defect for another.

So the bridge mirrors the theme's own reach instead of guessing an element: the app
viewport, and every skin-carrying element inside it. `[class*="neo-theme-"]` is
precisely the set `:root .neo-theme-*` can match, so both rules always evaluate on the
same elements and this one is (0,3,0) against (0,2,0). No per-skin duplication, and no
`!important` — the theme layer would only tie at (0,2,0) and resolve on load order,
which #17241 already records is not a contract.

Also projects #17963's new `--tab-header-*` family, which was never bridged: its eight
tokens landed on an already-inert bridge, which is why the design pass read as
"nothing changed" in the app it named as its living witness.

The spec asserts computed values on the CONSUMING elements against the palette entry
each token maps to — never a literal, so a palette retune stays green. A class check
could not substitute: the skin class was never missing. Red-proof on the pre-fix tree:
3 of 4 red, `--grid-container-border-color` received `#1d2e62` against `#262f3d`.
The fourth — the grid header button block, deliberately untouched — stays green in
both trees, so it doubles as the no-change control.

Co-Authored-By: Vega <neo-opus-vega@neomjs.com>

* test(workstation): the bridge census covers every declaration, not the easy ones (#17984)

Discharges RA-1. The bridge declares 21 custom properties; the witness read 13 direct
plus one composed band. The PR and ticket both claim "every bridged token", and a claim
wider than its instrument is exactly the defect class this spec exists for.

The seven missing were not a random sample. Six are COMPOSED values — `color-mix()`
mixes and a border shorthand — which the old palette-equality helper could not express,
so the census had quietly shrunk to the tokens that were easy to assert. Each row now
carries an `expect(palette)` function instead of a palette key, so a composed value is
as assertable as a direct one and a palette retune still cannot make the arm stale.

The seventh is `--tab-button-background-color`, and it is the one declaration this spec
cannot discriminate: the app and both neo themes independently arrive at `transparent`,
so deleting the bridge does not move it. It is carried in the census with that stated
rather than dropped — an unlisted token reads as an oversight, a listed
non-discriminating one reads as a measurement.

That disposition is asserted, not narrated. The mutation arm now compares the SET of
tokens that move against the set expected to move, rather than a count: a count tolerates
one token going quiet while another unexpectedly moves, and the set names which
declaration changed character. Measured: 20 of 21 move, and the twenty-first is the one
named above. If a theme ever changes that value, the arm reds and the census gains a
discriminating member.

Red-proof at the pre-fix SCSS, spec unchanged: 3 of 4 red. The fourth is the
grid-header-button no-change control, green on both trees as before.
